# Events

<!-- Generated from crates/koru-events/src/registry.rs. Do not edit by hand;
     run `KORU_UPDATE_EVENTS=1 cargo test -p koru-events` to regenerate. -->

**Every event this system publishes, and what each one is for.** One registry,
in `crates/koru-events/src/registry.rs`, which the code compiles against — so a
name that is not a row here cannot be sent, and this table cannot drift from
what is emitted.

Read the columns as: what happened (**Event**), which payload shape (**v** —
bumped only on a breaking change, and a `(name, version)` pair is never reused
with a different meaning), what kind of fact it is (**Class**), whether it may
leave the machine (**Telemetry**), and the typed values it carries
(**Attributes**).

**Class** is `domain` — something happened to content, kept 90 days — or
`instrumentation` — an observation about the app, kept 14. **Telemetry** is
`operational` (exportable service health), `anonymous-usage` or `pseudonymous-usage`
(exportable product measurement), `local-reference` (never leaves), or `never`.

**Attributes are typed and there is no string.** A value is an `id`, a `time`,
a `token` from a closed vocabulary the row declares, a `count`, an `int`, a
`version`, a `bucket` or a `flag` — so content cannot be smuggled through one.
Before anything is exported, every `id` and every `local-reference` attr, and
all actor, device, profile, workspace and subject identity, are stripped
mechanically — whatever the telemetry policy says.

**To add or change an event**, add the row and regenerate; never write a bare
name at a call site. An attribute an exportable policy would ship needs a
privacy-class review first.

What an event *is*, and where it goes: [README.md](../docs/architecture/eventbus/README.md).
What is still owed: [AGENTIC_FLOWS.md](../docs/architecture/eventbus/AGENTIC_FLOWS.md).

| Event | v | Class | Telemetry | Attributes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reminder.rule.changed` | 1 | domain | never | — | A synchronized reminder rule or its monotonic deletion fact changed. Content-free and profile-scoped; consumers re-read the authoritative reconciliation snapshot. |
| `reminder.action.appended` | 1 | domain | never | — | A synchronized occurrence action was appended. Content-free and profile-scoped; the action and reminder are read from authoritative state. |
| `reminder.history.cleared` | 1 | domain | never | — | Handled reminder history was explicitly cleared. Content-free and profile-scoped; active and snoozed actions were untouched. |
| `reminder.settings.changed` | 1 | domain | never | — | End-of-day or default-tone reminder settings changed. Content-free and profile-scoped. |
| `profile.dictionary.changed` | 1 | domain | never | — | The synchronized personal spelling dictionary changed. Content-free and profile-scoped; consumers re-read the authoritative private Profile unit. |
| `due.changed` | 1 | domain | never | `entity_id` : id/local-reference | A projected koru.due value was set, moved, or cleared. Derived from the unthrottled semantic projection diff; ids only, and consumers re-read current state. |
| `entity.removed` | 1 | domain | never | `entity_id` : id/local-reference | A previously projected entity disappeared from a current document projection. This observed transition is a cleanup wake, never permission to infer deletion from a cold projection. |
| `document.created` | 1 | domain | anonymous-usage | — | A document exists that did not before. Derived by the events worker from the store's commit feed (first sight of the document in doc_state); subject = the document. On a fresh journal the baseline seeding pass suppresses this for documents that already existed. |
| `document.updated` | 1 | domain | anonymous-usage | — | A known document's content changed. Derived from the commit feed and THROTTLED: at most one per document per 15 minutes, so it means 'was edited around then', never 'one edit'. Consumers wanting every commit belong on the store's own feed. |
| `document.removed` | 1 | domain | never | — | A document was dropped for good — not binned. Trash is a move (document.trashed); this is the end of the id. |
| `document.trashed` | 1 | domain | never | — | A document was moved to the trash. It still resolves and can be restored; subject = the document. |
| `document.restored` | 1 | domain | never | — | A document came back out of the trash. |
| `workspace.created` | 1 | domain | anonymous-usage | `source` : token/exact-categorical (onboarding \| manual \| import) | The app created a workspace. Emitted at the creation call sites (the app knows the source; the store layer cannot tell creation from first sight); subject = the workspace. |
| `workspace.observed` | 1 | domain | anonymous-usage | — | A workspace became visible on this device that the journal had never seen — derived by the events worker from the commit feed, so it covers every writer: this app, a phone, an MCP tool, a direct API client, or a peer's workspace arriving by sync. Deliberately NOT `workspace.created`: the store layer cannot tell creation from first sight, and a workspace synced from another device was not created here. `workspace.created` remains the app's own precise signal, carrying the `source` only it knows; the two answer different questions and are not a double count of one. |
| `workspace.deleted` | 1 | domain | anonymous-usage | — | The app deleted a workspace — a soft delete the store purges after its retention window, so restoring one is possible and does not un-say this. Emitted at the delete call sites; subject = the workspace. |
| `task.created` | 1 | domain | never | `reason` : token/exact-categorical (explicit \| due \| tasks_view)<br>`node_kind` : token/exact-categorical (paragraph \| task \| document \| image \| file) | A node became a task. Emitted by the `ensure_task` and `set_due` canonical commands — `set_due` on a plain row both creates and dates it, so one gesture is a `created` and a `due.changed` sharing one correlation. |
| `task.removed` | 1 | domain | never | — | A node stopped being a task — Remove from Tasks. The node and its content stay; only the task state goes. Emitted by `remove_from_tasks`. |
| `task.completed` | 1 | domain | never | `reason` : token/exact-categorical (explicit_complete \| checkbox_completed \| cascade_from_ancestor) | A task was completed. Emitted by `complete_task` ONCE PER TASK, including each task the cascade completed below it — a cascade is a set of events sharing one correlation, not one event with a count. |
| `task.reopened` | 1 | domain | never | `reason` : token/exact-categorical (explicit_reopen \| checkbox_reopened \| unfinished_child_added) | A completed task is open again. Emitted by `reopen_task` and by the classification pass — one per task, so a reopen chain up the ancestors is several events under one correlation. |
| `task.due.changed` | 1 | domain | never | `change` : token/exact-categorical (set \| changed \| cleared)<br>`temporal_kind` : token/exact-categorical (date \| datetime_zoned \| none) | A task's Due changed. Emitted by `set_due` and `clear_due`. It says THAT a deadline moved and what shape it now has, and deliberately not what it is — no date, in any spelling, ever enters an event. |
| `task.priority.changed` | 1 | domain | never | `change` : token/exact-categorical (set \| changed \| cleared)<br>`priority?` : token/exact-categorical (low \| medium \| high \| urgent) | A task's Priority changed. Emitted by the priority door and ONLY when the target already `is_task` — setting a priority on a plain row is not task activity and creates no task. |
| `task.child.added` | 1 | domain | never | `child` : id/local-reference<br>`child_class` : token/exact-categorical (unfinished_structural \| finished_structural \| passive)<br>`reopened` : flag/exact-categorical | A child was inserted under a task. Emitted by the classification pass from an insert. A faithful import emits nothing — imports are restore, not editing, and run through the named exemption. |
| `task.child.moved` | 1 | domain | never | `child` : id/local-reference<br>`child_class` : token/exact-categorical (unfinished_structural \| finished_structural \| passive)<br>`reopened` : flag/exact-categorical | A child moved under a task. Emitted by the classification pass from a move — the same three attrs as an insert, because from the task's side the two are the same news arriving differently. |
| `task.child.removed` | 1 | domain | never | `child` : id/local-reference | A child left a task — deleted, or moved away. Emitted by the structural delete/move-away hook. It carries no class: what the child was is what the `added` event already said, and a departure never reopens anything. |
| `task.child.completed` | 1 | domain | never | `child` : id/local-reference<br>`child_is_task` : flag/exact-categorical | Something under a task was completed. Emitted by `complete_task` on a node whose NEAREST task ancestor exists — one event for that ancestor, never one per ancestor up the tree. |
| `task.child.reopened` | 1 | domain | never | `child` : id/local-reference<br>`child_is_task` : flag/exact-categorical<br>`reopened_parent` : flag/exact-categorical | Something under a task was reopened. Emitted by `reopen_task` and by the checkbox-driven reopen, for the nearest task ancestor. |
| `task.content.changed` | 1 | domain | never | — | A task's own text was edited. COALESCED, and the boundary is part of the contract: one event per task per editing BURST. Four constraints, none of them negotiable by an emitter — NEVER PER KEYSTROKE (the burst set is a map the edit path inserts into; emission reads it); NO TIMER OF ITS OWN (it rides the host's existing throttled maintenance tick — nothing in this feature may put a new clock on the idle path); NO DOCUMENT WALK (the set names the nodes that changed; nothing scans for them); and NEVER THE TEXT, which is why this row has no attrs at all. The desktop host wrapper owns the coalescing and a burst on a task ends at the first of: the caret leaving its row, the maintenance tick seeing five quiet seconds, or its tab closing. The MCP wrapper's burst is THE CALL — one per `edit_document` that changed a task's own text. It belongs to no command, so it carries neither correlation nor causation: it is its own root. |

The actor is whoever asked: a person, or the orchestrator for a scheduled firing. |

One per attempt: a resume is a new attempt and a new row. |

Recorded by the recovering orchestrator, so it is timestamped at recovery, not at the crash. |

An orchestrator turn's failure fails the run; a human turn's is recorded and never terminalizes (§7.5). |

| `profile.appearance_changed` | 1 | domain | never | `profile` : id/local-reference | A profile's switcher icon or named colour changed — either here (`PATCH /v1/profiles/{id}/appearance`) or on another device, arriving through peer or Cloud sync. The icon and the colour name are absent: a banner refetches the record rather than reading it off the bus, which is what keeps this an invalidation signal and not a second copy of the catalog. |
| `document.private.changed` | 1 | domain | never | `profile` : id/local-reference | One reader's device-local private view state for one document — which toggles they closed — committed a change through `PATCH /v1/profiles/{id}/documents/{document}/private-state`. | `workspace.catalog.created` | 1 | domain | never | — | The Store committed a new workspace record and its manifest (`POST /v1/workspaces`); subject = the workspace. | `workspace.catalog.renamed` | 1 | domain | never | — | A workspace's name changed in the catalog and in its manifest (`PATCH /v1/workspaces/{id}`); subject = the workspace. The name itself never crosses — it is content, and no AttrKind holds it. |
| `workspace.catalog.appearance_changed` | 1 | domain | never | — | A committed `PATCH /v1/workspaces/{id}/appearance` — the whole set (icon, colour, pinned, archived) is sent every time, so this is one event per accepted request and never one per field. It is the *invalidation* signal for a switcher; when the request also flipped `archived`, the lifecycle fact rides beside it as `workspace.catalog.archived` or `.unarchived`, because a surface that must act immediately on an archive should not have to refetch to discover it did. |
| `workspace.catalog.archived` | 1 | domain | never | — | A workspace became archived — the false-to-true transition only, read from the record before and after the same committed appearance write. Re-sending `archived: true` for a workspace that already was says nothing, because nothing changed. Archiving hides a workspace and its projects; it mutates no project record. |
| `workspace.catalog.unarchived` | 1 | domain | never | — | The same transition the other way. Deliberately not `workspace.catalog.restored`: that one is the end of a soft delete, and archive and soft-delete are independent axes on the record (`archived: bool`, `deleted_at: Option<Timestamp>`), not two names for one state. |
| `workspace.catalog.deleted` | 1 | domain | never | — | The Store soft-deleted a workspace (`DELETE /v1/workspaces/{id}`) — recoverable until the retention window purges it; subject = the workspace. Emitted only when the delete committed: a request refused because live connections hold the workspace emits nothing. |
| `workspace.catalog.restored` | 1 | domain | never | — | A soft-deleted workspace came back (`POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/restore`); subject = the workspace. Its hidden projects reappear with no project mutation. |
| `workspace.catalog.moved` | 1 | domain | never | `from_profile` : id/local-reference<br>`to_profile` : id/local-reference | A workspace's owning profile changed (`POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/move`); subject = the workspace. Its id, its name, its documents and its history are untouched — only the owner and its position in the destination's order. Emitted only when the reassignment committed; a request refused because the target profile does not exist emits nothing. |
